artists.biography: Xavier Amin Dphrepaulezz (born January 20, 1968), better known by his stage name Fantastic Negrito, is an American singer-songwriter whose music spans blues, R&B, and roots music. His 2016 album The Last Days of Oakland won a Grammy award for Best Contemporary Blues Album at the 59th Grammy Awards. In 2019, his album Please Don't Be Dead won the same category for the 61st Grammy Awards. His 2020 album, Have You Lost Your Mind Yet? won Fantastic Negrito his 3rd consecutive Best Contemporary Blues Album Grammy at the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards.

Fantastic Negrito.biography: Xavier Amin Dphrepaulezz (born January 20, 1968), better known by his stage name Fantastic Negrito, is an American singer-songwriter whose music spans blues, R&B, and roots music. His 2016 album The Last Days of Oakland won a Grammy award for Best Contemporary Blues Album at the 59th Grammy Awards. In 2019, his album Please Don't Be Dead won the same category for the 61st Grammy Awards. His 2020 album, Have You Lost Your Mind Yet? won Fantastic Negrito his 3rd consecutive Best Contemporary Blues Album Grammy at the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards.

perplexity.description:
The Last Days of Oakland is the 2016 full-length debut album by Fantastic Negrito, released on Blackball Universe Records. The album blends raw blues, gritty rock, and roots music into a sound that is both urgent and soulful. Drawing from the legacy of bluesmen like Skip James and infused with punk energy, Fantastic Negrito—real name Xavier Dphrepaulezz—delivers a collection of songs that reflect his personal struggles and the changing landscape of his hometown, Oakland. Tracks such as "Working Poor," "Lost in a Crowd," and "The Nigga Song" showcase his ability to merge autobiographical storytelling with social commentary, creating a sound that is both deeply personal and politically resonant.

This album marks a pivotal moment in Fantastic Negrito’s career, establishing him as a major voice in contemporary blues and roots music after years away from the spotlight. The Last Days of Oakland received widespread critical acclaim for its authenticity and emotional depth, earning the Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Blues Album in 2017. Its success set the stage for a string of acclaimed follow-ups, solidifying Fantastic Negrito’s reputation as an artist who bridges the past and present of American music.
